head: 02b434d87d96
postReferenceChange: The only skill-tree change after 19538de0 is the PDF rename from 2026_ Prelim_P1.pdf to 2026_Prelim_P1.pdf.
recommendation: Fix the checker’s unsafe expression parsing and empty-check behavior before relying on it. The written workflow is strong, but scripts and commit/output side effects need safeguards.

findings.title: Math expressions execute arbitrary Python
findings.evidence: A controlled check expression created a /tmp marker through sympy.sympify; the checker reported PASS and exited 0.
findings.impact: Running checks derived from user- or model-supplied content can execute code with the agent process’s permissions.
findings.recommendation: Do not pass untrusted strings to sympify. Parse a tightly restricted expression grammar, validate the JSON schema and expression size, and add a regression test for code-execution payloads.

findings.title: An empty verification suite passes
findings.evidence: With {"checks": []}, the script prints ‘0/0 checks passed.’ and exits 0, although SKILL.md G4 requires at least two independent checks.
findings.impact: A caller can receive a successful process status without having verified any claim.
findings.recommendation: Reject missing, malformed, and empty check lists; enforce a non-zero minimum (and keep the skill’s two-independent-check requirement at the workflow gate).

findings.title: Delivery instructs an unrequested Git commit
findings.evidence: G6 says to make a Conventional Commit whenever a Git repository is available, without requiring explicit user authorization or checking the staged file set.
findings.impact: An answer-generation or audit request can mutate repository history; a careless implementation may include unrelated staged work. This also conflicts with G5’s ‘no unrequested rewrite’ gate.
findings.recommendation: Commit only when explicitly requested. Before any authorized commit, inspect status and stage only the generated deliverable.

findings.title: Textless PDFs fail open without an OCR or visual fallback
findings.evidence: A generated one-page textless PDF produced an empty pages.txt and a normal ‘Wrote…’ message with exit code 0; the fidelity report did not warn that no question text was extracted.
findings.impact: Scanned pages can appear successfully processed even though no source text was ingested, undermining G0/G1 fidelity checks.
findings.recommendation: Fail or emit a prominent per-page no-text status, then require OCR or direct visual inspection before the workflow can pass G0.

findings.title: Default extraction outputs overwrite existing files
findings.evidence: Running against an output directory containing sentinel pages.txt and fidelity_report.txt replaced both files without warning.
findings.impact: A repeat run can destroy previously extracted evidence or unrelated files with the same names.
findings.recommendation: Refuse to overwrite existing output files by default, or write to a unique run directory and use an explicit overwrite option.

findings.title: The fidelity heuristic is noisy and stdout is truncated
findings.evidence: On the 24-page supplied PDF, the report emitted 343 ‘orphan 1’ hits (including ordinary page/mark/numeral text); stdout prints only the first 4,000 report characters. Q6’s missing modulus bars and conjugate markers were nevertheless flagged.
findings.impact: High false-positive volume makes genuine symbol-loss warnings harder to prioritize; later findings can be hidden in terminal output.
findings.recommendation: Use context-aware, topic-scoped patterns; distinguish candidate flags from confirmed defects; print a truncation notice and report path when output is shortened.

findings.title: The corrected exemplar still omits two stated delivery checks
findings.evidence: The corrected answer cites page 4 and labels transcription/mark-split confidence well, but does not record the cover-page accuracy rules verbatim or include the explicit verified/deferred handoff required by G0/G6.
findings.impact: The exemplar is strong mathematically but does not demonstrate every mandatory workflow gate, which weakens it as a conformance reference.
findings.recommendation: Add the relevant cover instruction (3 significant figures for non-exact values; 1 decimal place for angles in degrees) and an explicit verified/deferred handoff, or mark those items not applicable with a reason.

verification.evidence: Clean main branch at 02b434d87d96. Since 19538de0, only the sample PDF filename changed to remove an embedded space.
lint_skill.py reports a 163-line body and valid structure/frontmatter/local links.
Rendered PDF page 4 and solution pages 16–18; confirmed the modulus bars, conjugate, fraction modulus, 0 < arg(a) < π/2, cover accuracy rules, and official Q6 results.

Exact SymPy checks covered the Cartesian reduction, circle membership, substitution into the original modulus equation, equal-distance line, tangency discriminant, first-quadrant angle, and part (b) tangent point.
A controlled expression created a temporary marker via sympify; no repository files were changed.
An empty checks list reported 0/0 passed with exit code 0.
The extractor found Q6’s symbol-loss candidates, but silently accepted a textless PDF and overwrote existing output files in isolated tests.

sampleAssessment.original: The main Q6 results are correct, but the answer links an external diagram, has a dangling ‘Hence,’ before the circle form, and includes a ‘3 not 3²’ correction that the corrected file’s own change log calls bogus. It also lacks the required verification ledger and omits some explicit domain/branch checks.
sampleAssessment.corrected: The v2 answer matches the bound solutions and its exact claims pass 7/7 independent checks. It removes the external link and bogus correction, clarifies notation, shows the circle equation, checks the principal range and denominator, and supplies an evidence ledger. Its source/mark-confidence labels are appropriately cautious.
sampleAssessment.limitation: The original user prompt that preceded model_answer_6.md is not present in the repository, so the claim about what the user pasted cannot be independently compared. The PDF includes worked solutions, not a detailed mark scheme; per-step credit remains indicative.

overallAssessment: The skill has a strong, well-matched exam workflow: source fidelity before solving, command-word obligations, exact working, original-condition checks, explicit confidence, and a useful answer audit rubric. The supplied corrected answer demonstrates that these practices improve the sample substantially. The helper scripts and unconditional commit instruction are not production-safe as written; fix the High/Medium findings before relying on automated verification or repository delivery.
